68:1: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of His saying N. Some of them said: It is the whale on which the earths rest. It was mentioned by the one who said that: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The first thing that God created was the pen, so it wrote what would be, then He raised the water vapor, and from it the heavens were created, then He created the letter Nun, and the earth was spread out on the back of the letter Nun, so the earth moved and swayed, and it was fixed by the mountains, for the mountains boast of the earth. He said: And he recited: Nun, by the pen and what they write. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, or Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Abbas, in a similar manner, except that he said: Then the heavens were split from it. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us: Sufyan told us: Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The first thing that God created was the pen. He said: Write. He said: What should I write? He said: Write the destiny. He said: So it wrote what would happen from that day until the Hour of Resurrection. Then He created the Nun and raised the water vapor, so the heavens burst forth from it and the earth was spread out on the back of the Nun. The Nun was compelled, so the earth shook, and He established the mountains, so they boast of being above the earth.” Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la narrated: Muhammad ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing that God created was the pen. Then He said to it: Write. It said: What should I write? It said: Write the destiny. He said: So the pen wrote down what would happen until the Day of Resurrection. Then He lifted up the water vapor and split the heavens from it. Then He created the nun, and the earth was spread out on its back. The nun was compelled, and the earth shook, and it was fixed with the mountains, and they boast over the earth. Wasil bin Abdul A’la told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, that Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr told him on the authority of Mujahid, he said: It was said: The Nun is the whale that is under the seventh earth. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, he said: Muammar said: Al-A’mash told us, that Ibn Abbas said: The first thing created was the pen. Then he mentioned a hadith similar to that of Wasil on the authority of Ibn Fadil, and he added to it: Then Ibn Abbas recited: “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.” Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha Muslim ibn Subaih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing my Lord created was the pen. He said to it: Write, so it wrote what will be until the Hour comes. Then He created the letter Nun above the water, then He pressed the earth down upon it. Others said: N is one of the letters of the Most Gracious. Who said that? Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Marwazi told us: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us: My father told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Alif, Lam, Meem, and Noon are the letters of the Most Gracious, separated. Muhammad bin Muammar told me, he said: Abbas bin Ziyad al-Bahili told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement al-Raw, al-Ha-Mim, al-Nun, he said: It is a disjointed noun. Others said: N is the inkwell, and al-Qalam is the pen. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Yaqub told us, he said: My brother Isa bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Bunani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God created the nun, which is the inkwell, and created the pen, and said: Write, and it said: What should I write? He said: Write down what will happen until the Day of Resurrection, of deeds done, righteous or wicked, or the provision allocated, lawful or unlawful. Then He made obligatory for each thing its nature, its entry into the world and its duration in it, and its exit from it. Then He appointed guardians over the servants, and storers for the book. The guardians copy every day from the storers the work of that day. Then when the provision is exhausted and the trace is cut off, and the term expires, the guardians come to the storers asking for the work of that day. The storers say to them: We do not find anything for your companion with us. Then the storers return and find that they have died. Ibn Abbas said: Are you not an Arab people who hear the storers say: Indeed, we were copying what you did (al-Jathiyah 45:29). And can copying be anything other than from an original? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatada, regarding his statement N, he said: It is the inkwell. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: The letter nun means the inkwell. Others said: N: a tablet of light. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Shabil Al-Maktab told us: Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Jazari told us, on the authority of Furat bin Abi Al-Furat, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Farah, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe”: A tablet of light that records what will happen until the Day of Resurrection. Others said: N is an oath that God swears by. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe,” God swears by whatever He wills. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe,” he said: This is an oath by which God swore. Others said: It is one of the names of the Surah. Others said: It is a letter of the alphabet. We have already mentioned the statement regarding similar letters of the alphabet that begin the beginnings of the surahs, and the statement regarding his statement is similar to the statement regarding that. The reciters differed in the reading of Nun. The majority of the reciters of Kufa pronounced the nun in it and in Ya Seen, except for al-Kisa’i and the majority of the reciters of Basra, because it is a letter of the alphabet, and the alphabet is based on stopping on it even if it is connected. Al-Kisa’i would assimilate the last nun of them and conceal it based on the connection. The correct statement regarding this, in our view, is that they are two eloquent readings, and whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. However, the pronunciation of the letter nun is more eloquent and well-known, and I like it better. As for the pen, it is the well-known pen. However, the pen by which our Lord swore was the pen that God, the Most High, created, and He commanded it to write down everything that will be until the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad ibn Salih al-Anmati told me, saying: Ibad ibn al-Awam told us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Salim told us, saying: I heard Ata’ say: I asked al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit: What was your father’s last will and testament when death gathered him? He said: He called me and said: O my son, fear God, and know that you will never fear God and you will never attain knowledge until you believe in God alone and in destiny, both its good and its bad. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The first thing God created was the pen, and He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what should I write? He said: Write destiny. The pen wrote at that moment what was and what will be until eternity. Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Tusi told me: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq told us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us: Rabah ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Habib, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Or is it that God created the pen and commanded it to write down everything? Musa bin Sahl al-Ramli told us: Na’im bin Hammad told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us with his chain of transmission, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Some people lie about predestination. He said: They lie about the Book of God. I will take hold of one of their hairs and not cut it short. God was on His Throne before He created anything. The first thing He created was the pen, which recorded what would happen until the Day of Resurrection. People only act on a matter that has already been completed. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad told us: Shu’bah told us: Abu Hashim told us that he heard Mujahid say: I heard Abdullah - we do not know whether it was Ibn Umar or Ibn Abbas - say: The first thing God created was the pen, and the pen wrote down what would happen. People today only work on what it has finished. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, and Abdullah ibn Adam told me, he said: My father told us, he said: Al-Layth ibn Saad told us, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Salih, on the authority of Ayoub ibn Ziyad, he said: Ibad ibn al-Walid ibn al-Samit told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My father Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: O my son, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The first thing God created was the pen, and He said to it: Write, and it wrote down in that instant what would happen until the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Nun and the pen, he said: that with which the remembrance was written. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he told him on the authority of Ibrahim Ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Nun and the Pen, he said: That with which the remembrance was written. And his statement: And what they write means: and what they write and inscribe. If the interpretation is directed in this way, then the oath is by creation and their actions. The statement may have another meaning, which is that its meaning is: and they wrote what they write, so what is in the sense of a source. If the interpretation is directed in this way, then the oath is by the book, as if it was said: Nun, the pen, and the book. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And what they write down he said: And what they write down. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, and what they write, meaning: they write. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And what they write, he said: And what they write. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And what they write down means what they write down. It is said from this: So-and-so wrote down the book, so he writes down a line: if he wrote it. And from this is the saying of Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj: I and Astar wrote a line
68:2: And His saying: You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman, thereby disbelieving the polytheists of Quraysh who said to him: You are mad.
68:3: And His statement: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted. God Almighty says: And indeed, O Muhammad, for you is a great reward from God for your patience in the face of the harm that the polytheists inflicted upon you, neither diminished nor cut off. This is from their saying: a weak rope, meaning it is weak. And its strength has weakened: meaning its strength has weakened. Mujahid used to say about this: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, not grateful, he said: counted.
68:4: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And indeed, O Muhammad, you are on a great path, and that is the path of the Qur’an with which God taught him, which is Islam and its laws. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And indeed, you are of a great moral character, meaning: a great religion. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And indeed, you are of a great moral character, meaning: You are of a great religion, which is Islam. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a great creation, he said: religion. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: His character was the Qur’an, saying as it is in the Qur’an. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And indeed, you are of a great moral character. It was mentioned to us that Saeed bin Hisham asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: Do you not read the Qur’an? He said: I said: Yes. She said: Indeed, the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur’an. Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas told us: My father told us: Al-Mubarak ibn Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Saeed ibn Hisham, who said: I came to Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, and I said: Tell me about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: His character was the Qur’an. Do you not read: And indeed, you are of a great moral character? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Abu al-Zahariyyah, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayl, he said: So I went to Aisha and asked her about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: The character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur’an. Ubaid bin Asbat told us: My father told me, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah, regarding his statement, And indeed, you are of a great moral character, he said: The etiquette of the Qur’an. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, He is of a great moral character, meaning his religion and his affair that he was upon, from what he was commanded to do, from what God commanded him to do and entrusted him to.
68:5: And His statement, Then you will see, and they will see * which of you is afflicted. God Almighty says: Then you will see, O Muhammad, and the polytheists of your people who call you mad will see, which of you is afflicted. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Then you will see, and they will see, meaning: You will see, and they will see.
68:6: And his statement, Which of you is the one who is afflicted? The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its interpretation is which of you is the madman, as if he directed the meaning of the preposition with in his statement, with which of you to the meaning of in. And if you direct the preposition with to the meaning of in, then the interpretation of the statement is: And they see which of the two groups is the madman, in your group, O Muhammad, or their group. And the madman is a noun raised by the preposition with. Mention of who said the meaning of that: Which of you is crazy? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: Which of you is bewitched? He said: The insane. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: Which of you is bewitched? He said: Which of you is insane. Others said: Rather, the interpretation of that is: Which of you is crazy? It is as if those who said this statement directed the one who is being tempted to the meaning of temptation or temptations, just as it was said: He has no reason or conviction: meaning he has no mind or conviction of opinion. So in the same way, the one who is being tempted was placed in the place of temptations. It was mentioned that: The infatuated means the source and means madness. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Which of you is afflicted? He said: Satan. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Which of you is afflicted? He meant madness. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He says: Which of you is mad? Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Which of you is more deserving of the devil? So, according to these people, the preposition ba is an addition, whether it enters or exits, and the example of these people is the saying of the rajaz poet: We are the Banu Ja'dah, the owners of the falaj. We strike with the sword and hope for relief. Meaning: We hope for relief. For them, the inclusion of the letter ba in this position and its exclusion are the same. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then you will see, and they will see * Which of you is the one who is afflicted, he said: Which of you is more deserving of the devil. The Arabists differed on this matter in the same way that the commentators differed. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of this is: Then you will see and they will see which of you is the one who is afflicted. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Which of you is afflicted here, meaning madness, and it is in the doctrine of afflictions, as they said: It has no rational or binding basis. He said: If you wish, you can make which of you into which of you in which of the two groups is the madman. He said: In that case, it is a noun, not a source. The first and most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: Which of you is mad? The direction of the one who is afflicted to the fitun in the sense of the source, because that is the most obvious meaning of the speech, if he did not intend to drop the ba’, and we made an understandable way for its inclusion, and we have explained that it is not permissible for there to be something in the Qur’an that has no meaning.
68:7: And His statement: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way means, the Most High said: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, like the straying of the infidels of Quraysh from the religion of God and the path of guidance. And He is most knowing of the guided ones means: And He is most knowing of the guided ones, who followed the truth and acknowledged it, just as you were guided and followed the truth. This is from the metaphors of speech, but the meaning of the speech is: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing, O Muhammad, of you, and you are the guided one, and of your people from the infidels of Quraysh and that they are the ones who have gone astray from the path of truth.
68:8: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So do not obey, O Muhammad, those who deny the signs of God and His Messenger. They wish that you would compromise so that they would compromise. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Those who deny the signs of God wish that you would disbelieve in God, O Muhammad, so that they would disbelieve.
68:9: Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, If you were to compromise, they would be compliant, meaning: They would wish you would disbelieve, so they would disbelieve. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, They wish that you would compromise so that they would compromise, that he said: You would disbelieve so that they would disbelieve. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: They wish you would compromise so they would compromise. He said: You would disbelieve so they would disbelieve. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They would like you to make things easy for them so they would make things easy for them, or you would be lenient in your religion so they would be lenient in their religion. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, If you were to compromise, they would compromise, meaning: If you were to make things easy for them, they would make things easy. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They wish that you would compromise so they would compromise, he said: If you were to give in to their gods and leave them some of the truth, they would be content with you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, They wish that you would compromise so they would compromise, meaning: They wish, O Muhammad, that you would compromise on this matter, so they would compromise with you. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, They wish that you would compromise so that they would compromise, he said: They wish that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would compromise so that they would compromise. The more correct of the two opinions on this is the opinion of those who said: The meaning of this is: These polytheists, O Muhammad, would like you to be lenient with them in your religion by responding to their request to incline to their gods, so that they would be lenient with you in your worship of your God, as God Almighty said: “And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little. Then We would have made you taste double the [expectation of] life and double the [expectation of] death.” It is taken from fat, similar to softening in the saying about softening of fat.
68:10: And his saying, And do not obey every worthless swearer. And do not obey, O Muhammad, every one who frequently swears falsely, worthless: he is weak. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that, except that some of them directed the meaning of humiliated to the liar, and I think that he did that because he saw that if he is described as humiliated, then he is only described with that because of the humiliation of his own soul that was upon him, and likewise the description of the liar, he only lies because of the humiliation of his own soul upon him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And do not obey every worthless oath-taker. The worthless one is the liar. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, a humiliating oath-taker, he said: It is weak. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And do not obey every worthless swearer, meaning one who commits many evil deeds. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Hasan regarding his statement, Every oath-taker is despised, he said: Every person who swears a lot is despised and weak. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Qatada: And do not obey every worthless swearer. He said: He is the one who commits many evil deeds.
68:11: And his saying slanderer means: a backbiter of people and a eater of their flesh. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying backbiter means backbiting. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: A slanderer eats the flesh of Muslims. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, a slanderer, he said: The slanderer is the one who slanders people with his hand and strikes them, but not with his tongue. And he recited, Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (al-Humazah 104:1), the one who slanders people with his tongue. And the root of slander is backbiting, so it was said of the backbiter: Humaiz, because he attacks people’s reputations with what they dislike, and that is backbiting them. His saying, He goes around spreading gossip, means: He goes around telling people about one another, transmitting their talk to one another. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: A slanderer eats the flesh of Muslims. A gossiper transmits stories from one person to another. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Walking around with gossip means walking around with lies. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Kalbi, regarding his statement, He went about spreading gossip, he said: He is al-Akhns ibn Shuraiq, and his origin is from Thaqif, and he is counted among the Banu Zuhrah.
68:12: And his saying, He prevents good, means: God Almighty says: He is miserly with money and withholds it from rights. His saying aggressor means: someone who is aggressive towards people. Sinful means: someone who is sinful towards his Lord. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, transgressor in his work, sinful towards his Lord.
68:13: And his saying ‘Atal means: He is ‘Atal, and ‘Atal’ is the harsh and severe in his disbelief, and every severe and strong person is called ‘Atal by the Arabs, and from it is the aggressive finger: And time becomes a sick trunk And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, ‘Atal means the severe hypocrite. Ishaq bin Wahb Al-Wasiti told me: Abu Amir Al-Aqdi told us: Zuhair bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Wahb Al-Dhamari, who said: The heavens and the earth weep over a man whose creation God perfected, whose stomach was spacious, and to whom He gave a morsel of this world, and then he is unjust to the people. That is the oppressive, wicked man. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair, who said: The ‘Atal’ is the gluttonous, drinker, strong, and powerful. He is placed on the scales, but not even a barley grain is weighed. The king will push seventy thousand of them into Hell at once. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, regarding his statement, After that, he became a strong sinner. He said: The strong one means the tough one. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, regarding his statement, After that, he became a sinner. He said: The sinner is the healthy one. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Katheer ibn al-Harith, on the authority of al-Qasim, the freedman of Muawiyah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the violent, wicked person. He said: The obscene, vile person.” Muawiyah said, and I told Ayyadh bin Abdullah Al-Fahri, on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar to that. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, He became a tyrant after that, he said: He was of bad character and of lowly character. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, He became a tyrant after that, Al-Hasan and Qatada said: He is the vulgar, mean, and corrupt person. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Atal, he said: He is the vulgar, mean, and greedy person. He said: Ibn Thaur narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The heavens weep over a servant whom God has made healthy in body, spacious in stomach, and given a portion of this world, yet people are unjust. That is the oppressive, wicked one.’” Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin. Al-Atal said: The correct and strong. Jaafar bin Muhammad Al-Bazuri told me: Abu Zakariya, who is Yahya bin Mus`ab, told us on the authority of `Umar bin Nafi`, who said: `Ikrimah was asked about Atal after that, a fornicator, and he said: That is the vile, infidel. Ali bin Al-Hassan Al-Azdi told me that Yahya, meaning Ibn Al-Yaman, told us on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab on the authority of Al-Hassan regarding his statement, After that, he became a tyrant, he said: The obscene, mean, and vile person. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The violent, mean, and obscene person. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Atal, he said: Very evil. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Atal He said: Atal means strong. “After that, a fornicator.” The meaning of after in this context is the meaning of with, and the interpretation of the statement is Atal after that and a fornicator: meaning with the fornicator. And his saying: Zanim and the Zanim in the speech of the Arabs: is the one who sticks to the people but is not one of them, and from it is the saying of Hassan bin Thabit: You are a bastard who has been hung on the Hashimites as a single cup is hung behind a rider. Another said: A bastard who doesn't know who his father is, a prostitute of low birth And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Zanim he said: The Zanim is the pretender, and it is said: The Zanim is a man who has a defect that he is known for, and it is said: He is Al-Akhns bin Shuraik Al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah, and some people from Banu Zuhrah claimed that the Zanim is: Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth Al-Zuhri, but he is not him. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: He is the adopted son. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Sulayman ibn Bilal told me, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, that he heard him say about this verse: He became a tyrant after that. Sa`id said: He is the one who sticks to the people but is not one of them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The zanim is the one who is known for evil, just as a sheep is known by its hump, the one who sticks. Others said: It is the one with a tail like a sheep’s tail. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said about the adulterer, he said: He was described, but he was not known until he was called an adulterer. He said: He had a mark on his neck by which he was known. Others said: He was an impostor. Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada’i told me: Ali ibn Asim told us: Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, After that, a slanderer, he said: The verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, And do not obey every worthless swearer, a slanderer, going about with calumnies. He said: We did not recognize it until After that, a slanderer was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: We recognized it as his slander like the slander of a sheep. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of the commentators, who said: It is the one who has a tail like the tail of a sheep. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: The base one: He said: He had a blemish at the base of his ear. It is said: He is the base one who is attached to lineage. Others said: It is suspicious. Who said that? Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, After that, he became a sinner, he said: Sinner is the suspicious person who is known for evil. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The fornicator is the one who is known for evil. Others said: He is the oppressor. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Zanim, he said: Unjust. Others said: He is the one who is known as his daughter. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sa`id Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said about the fornicator: the one who is known by his daughter. Abu Ishaq said: I heard the people say about the emirate of Ziyadah: the `atal is the usurper. Others said: He is rude and coarse. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, he said: I heard Shahr bin Hawshab say: He is the coarse, the glutton and the drinker of what is forbidden. Others said: It is a sign of disbelief. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, on the authority of Ibn Yaman, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: The adulterer is a sign of the unbeliever. Ibn Hamid told me: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: The adulterer is a sign of the unbeliever. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, that he used to say: The adulterer is known by this description just as a sheep is known. Others said: He is known for his meanness. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The zaneem is the one who is known for his meanness, just as a sheep is known by its hump. Others said: He is the wicked one. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, regarding his statement, After that, he became a sinner. He said: The sinner is the wicked one.
68:14: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement if he was so Abu Ja`far al-Madani and Hamza recited it َأن كان ذ مالas a question with two hamzas, and those who recited it turned to two aspects: One of them is that it is intended to rebuke this humiliating oath-taker, so it was said: Because this humiliating oath-taker had wealth and children “When Our verses are recited to him, he says, Legends of the ancients” and this is the more apparent of the two aspects, and the other is that it is intended by it, Because he had wealth and children, you would obey him, as a rebuke to whoever obeyed him, and after the rest of the reciters of Madinah, Kufa and Basra recited it:إن كان ذ مالas a statement without a question with one hamza, and its meaning if it is recited like that: And do not obey every humiliating oath-taker “if he had wealth and children” as if he forbade him from obeying him because he had wealth and children.
68:15: And His saying, When Our verses are recited to him, he says, ‘Legends of the ancients.’ He says: When the verses of Our Book are recited to him, he says, This is from what the ancients wrote, mocking him and denying that it was from God.
68:16: And his saying: We will brand him on the snout. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: We will brand him with the sword, and we will make that a lasting mark and a permanent mark on him as long as he lives. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, We will brand him on the snout. So he fought on the day of Badr, and he was cut off with the sword in the battle. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: We will make it something lasting. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying, We will brand him on the snout is a shin that does not leave the last letter on it. Others said: It will be marked on his nose. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, We will brand him on the snout. He said: We will brand him on the nose. The more correct of the two interpretations of this, in my opinion, is the one that says: The meaning of this is: We will make his matter clear so that they will know him, and it will not be hidden from them, just as the mark on the snout is not hidden. Qatada said: The meaning of this is: A disgrace that cannot be surpassed by the last thing on him. It may also be possible that he was struck by the sword, so the striking of the snout by the sword was combined with the explanation of his faults to the people. And by his saying We will brand him he means we will cauterize him. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: We will brand him with the mark of the people of Hellfire, meaning we will blacken his face. He said: Even though the nose is specifically mentioned as a mark, it is in the manner of the face, because some parts of the face lead to others. The Arabs say: By God, I will brand you with a mark that will not leave you, meaning the nose. He said: And some of them recited to me: I will brand him with a mark that will never leave him, just as the brand burns with the heat of the hottest day. Al-Najz: a disease that affects camels, so their noses are cauterized.
68:17: God Almighty means by His statement, Indeed, We tested them, that is, We tested the polytheists of Quraysh. He says: We examined them and tried them. As We tested the companions of the garden, that is, as We tested the companions of the garden. When they swore to harvest it in the morning, that is, when they swore to harvest some of its fruit in the morning.
68:18: And they do not make an exception: They do not say, God willing. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, No poor person shall enter it upon you today, he said: They were people from Abyssinia whose father had a garden from which he used to feed the poor. When their father died, his sons said, By God, our father was truly foolish when he fed the poor. So they swore that they would harvest it in the morning and not make any exceptions, nor would they feed a poor person. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, They will surely harvest it in the morning, he said: Paradise belonged to an old man, and he used to give charity. His sons used to forbid him from giving charity, but he used to hold back his sustenance for the year and spend and give charity from the excess. When their father died, they went to it in the morning and said, No poor person should enter it upon you today. He mentioned that the people of Paradise were people of the Book. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sa`d told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, We tested them as We tested the companions of the garden when they swore... the verse. He said: They were from the People of the Book. And severing means cutting. What is meant by his statement, that they may harvest it is that they may find its fruit. And from this is the statement of Imru’ al-Qais: I cut you off after Daad contacted me and Daad started to feel some anger
68:19: God Almighty says: A visitor from God’s command knocked on the door of these people’s paradise at night while they were asleep. In Arabic, the word tourist only occurs at night, and not during the day. They might say: I visited it during the day. Al-Farra’ mentioned that Abu Al-Jarrah recited to him: She extinguished it during the day and not at night, and her Lord was distracted by the pursuit of the camels. Rakhaal: are the female offspring of sheep. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about the meaning of that. Who said that? Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kurayb told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the flood: And a group from your Lord swept over it. He said: It is a command from God. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And a company from your Lord circulated around them while they were asleep. He said: A company from God circulated around them while they were asleep.
68:20: And his statement, So it became like a barren field. The people of interpretation differed as to what was meant by barren field. Some of them said: It meant the black night. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: So their garden became burnt and black like the blackness of a dark, pitch-black night. Who said that? Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar told me, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Our sheikh told us, on the authority of sheikhs from the tribe of Kalb, whose name was Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, So it became like a barren land, he said: Barren land means night. He said: Abu Amr bin al-Ala’, may God have mercy on him, said about that: Why don't you wake up early while my reproacher blames me and my heart is still awake, while the wound is not yet healed? He also said: Your dark night has become long, and it cannot be separated from the harsh morning. If I say Aqsha'a or Tanaha, clouds will come from every direction. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: It became like a land called Al-Sareem, known by this name. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Na’im ibn Abd al-Rahman told me that he heard Sa’id ibn Jubayr say: It is a land in Yemen called Dharwan, six miles from Sana’a.
68:21: God Almighty says: And they called to one another in the morning. God Almighty says: So these people, who are the people of Paradise, called to one another in the morning. He says: They called to one another in the morning. He says: After they had become morning.
68:22: Go to your tillage and that crop if you are harvesters he says: if you are harvesters of your crops.
68:23: So they set out, whispering to one another. He says: So they went to their field, whispering to one another.
68:24: That no poor person shall enter it today upon you. He says: And they whispered to each other, saying: That no poor person shall enter your Paradise today upon you. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And they called one another in the morning, ‘Go forth to your tillage if you should be sharp-shooters.’ So they went while they spoke in low tones, meaning, they whispered, that no poor person should enter it upon you today. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: When their father died, they went to her and said: No poor person should enter her today.
68:25: The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of hard in this place. Some of them said: It means: they have the ability and are desperate. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And they went forth in the morning, determined and able, he said: having ability. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding God’s statement, able to do so, he said: able to do so in themselves. He said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And they set out in the morning, determined and able, he said: With effort, or he said: With seriousness. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And they went forth in the morning, determined and able. The people went forth in the morning, determined and able to go to their Paradise. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And they set out in the morning with great determination. He said: With great determination in their matter. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, on hardship, able, on hardship, able in themselves. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They went ahead with their matter, having agreed upon it among themselves, kept it secret, and kept it to themselves. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid: And they set out in the morning, with great determination. He said: Their father had a field, and they were brothers, so they said: We will not feed a poor person from it until we know what comes out of it. And they set out in the morning, with great determination, on a matter that they had established among themselves. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, on a stubborn matter, he said: on a matter that is agreed upon. Hanad told us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, And they set out in the morning, determined and able. He said: On a matter of consensus. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They became poor and needy. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Al-Hasan said, regarding His statement, And they set out in the morning in a state of great need, he said: In a state of need. Others said: Rather, it means: with anger. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: And they set out in the morning with great anger and power. He said: With wrath. It seems that Sufyan went in his interpretation of this to something like the saying of Al-Ashab bin Ramila: Blacks bought and found hidden blacks, they fell on the lions’ blood Meaning: in anger. Some of the people of Al-Ma’ufa, who spoke Arabic from Basra, interpreted this as, They went out to prevent, and he directed it to the fact that it is from their saying: Haradat Al-Sana if there was no rain in it, and Haradat Al-Naqah if she had no milk, as the poet said: If she is angry or cries, turn away from another eyebrow and cover it with mud. This is a statement that we do not know of anyone from among the early scholars who said it, even if it has a basis. If that is the case and it is not permissible for us to go beyond what the evidence has agreed upon, then the only valid statement on that is one of the statements we mentioned from the people of knowledge. If that is the case, and what is known of the meaning of hard in the speech of the Arabs is the intention, from their saying: So-and-so has haraded so-and-so has haraded: if he intended his intention, and from that is the saying of the rajaz poet: And a flood came, which was from the command of God, and it raged like the raging of the enslaved Paradise. Meaning: He intended to intend it. It is true that the one who is more deserving of the interpretation of the verse is the one who said: The meaning of his saying and they went out in the morning with great determination is that they went out with a matter that they had intended and relied on, and kept it secret among themselves, capable of it in themselves.
68:26: God Almighty says: When these people reached their garden and saw its crops burned, they denied it and doubted it, whether it was their garden or not. Some of them said to their companions, thinking that they had forgotten the path to their garden and that the one they had seen was another: We, O people, have lost our way to our garden. One of them, who knew that it was their garden and that they had not strayed from the path, said: Rather, we, O people, are deprived. We have been deprived of the benefit of our garden by the loss of its crops. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So when they saw it, they said, ‘Indeed, we are astray.’ That is, we have lost our way.
68:27: Rather, we are deprived. Rather, we were rewarded, so we were deprived. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So when they saw it, they said, ‘Indeed, we are astray.’ Qatada said: They said, “We have lost our way. This is not our Paradise.” Some of them said, Rather, we are deprived. We have been deprived of our Paradise.
68:28: And his saying: He said the most just of them means: the most just of them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, The most just of them said, he said, The most just of them, and it is said, The best of them said, and he said in Al-Baqarah, And thus We have made you a just community (al-Baqarah 2:143), he said: The middle means justice. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, The most just of them said, meaning: the most just of them. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Furat bin Khallad told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid, He said, ‘the most just of them’: the most just of them. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, The most moderate of them said, he said: The most just of them. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id: “He said: The most just of them.” He said: The most just of them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, The most moderate of them said, meaning the most just of them in speech, and he was the quickest of the people to panic, and the best of them in returning. Did I not tell you, why do you not glorify God? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: “He said: The most just of them.” He said: The most just of them. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The most just of them said, meaning: The most just of them. And His saying, Did I not tell you, ‘Why do you not glorify God?’ He says: Why do you not make an exception when you say, We will surely triumph over it in the morning, and say, God willing. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Al-Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid: Why do you not glorify God? He said: It has reached me that it is an exception. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid, Did I not tell you, ‘Why do you not glorify God?’ He said: He says: You make an exception, so glorification was an exception for them.
68:29: God Almighty says: The companions of Paradise said: Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers in our failure to make an exception in our division and our resolve not to feed the poor from the fruits of our Paradise.
68:30: And His statement, So they turned to one another, blaming one another, God Almighty says: So they turned to one another, blaming one another for their negligence in what they had neglected regarding the exception, and their determination to continue as they had been in not feeding the poor from their garden.
68:31: And His saying, Woe to us! We were indeed transgressors. He says: The people of Paradise said: Woe to us! We were indeed banished, disobeying God’s command by abandoning the exception and glorification.
68:32: God Almighty says, informing us of what the people of Paradise said: Perhaps our Lord will replace it for us with something better than it by our repentance for our previous wrongdoing, with something better than our Paradise. Indeed, we are desirous of our Lord. He says: Indeed, we are desirous of our Lord that He replace our Paradise, which has perished, with something better than it.
68:33: The Almighty said, Such is the punishment. The Almighty says, “As We did with the garden of the people of the garden, when it became like a dry land because of the calamity and corrupting plague We sent upon it, We did with those who disobeyed Our command and disbelieved in Our messengers in this immediate world. “And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater.” Meaning, the punishment of the Hereafter for those who disobeyed their Lord and disbelieved in Him is greater on the Day of Resurrection than the punishment and torment of this world. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, “Such is the punishment. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew,” meaning by that the punishment of this world. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, God said, Such is the punishment, meaning the punishment of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Such is the punishment, he said: The punishment of this world, the destruction of their wealth: meaning the punishment of this world. His saying, If they had known, means: If these polytheists had known that God’s punishment for those who associate partners with Him is greater than His punishment for them in this world, they would have been deterred, repented, and turned back. But in doing so, they are ignorant and do not know.
68:34: God Almighty says: Indeed, for the righteous who fear God’s punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins are with their Lord gardens of pleasure meaning: gardens of eternal pleasure.
68:35: And His statement, Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals? God Almighty says: Shall We treat, O people, those who submitted to Me in obedience, humbled themselves before Me in servitude, and were humble before My commands and prohibitions, in My honor and blessings in the Hereafter like the criminals who acquired sins, committed transgressions, and disobeyed My commands and prohibitions? No! God will not do that.
68:36: And His saying, What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Do you consider the obedient servant of God and the disobedient servant of God equal in their honor? God Almighty says: Do not treat them equally, for they are not equal before God. Rather, the obedient servant has permanent honor, and the disobedient servant has permanent humiliation.
68:37: God Almighty says to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:O people, by your equality between Muslims and criminals in the honor of God, do you have a book sent down from God, brought to you by a messenger from among His messengers, that you have what you choose, so that you may study in it what you say. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Or have you a book in which you study? He said: In it is what you say you read: you study it. And he recited, Or have We given them a book so they have clear evidence from it? (Fatir 35:40)... to the end of the verse.
68:38: And His statement, Indeed, you will have therein whatever you choose, God Almighty says: In that matter, you will have whatever you choose for yourselves. This is a command from God, a rebuke to these people and a rebuke to them for what they were saying of falsehood and what they were wishing for of false hopes.
68:39: And his saying, Or do you have oaths from Us that will last until the Day of Resurrection? He says: Do you have oaths from Us that will last until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have what you judge, meaning that you will have your judgment? But the alif was broken from in because the lam entered into al-Naba 78:meaning, do you have oaths from Us that you will have your judgment?
68:40: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ask, O Muhammad, which of these polytheists has a firm oath against us by their rule until the Day of Resurrection? Leader means: guarantor of it. Among the Arabs, a leader is the guarantor and the one who speaks on behalf of the people. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Which of them is responsible for that? means: Which of them is responsible for that. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Ask them which of them is responsible for that, he said: Which of them is responsible for that?
68:41: And His statement, Or do they have partners? Then let them produce their partners, if they are truthful. God Almighty says: Do these people have partners in what they say and describe of the matters that they claim are theirs? Then let them produce their partners in that, if they are truthful in what they claim of partners.
68:42: God Almighty says, On the Day the shin will be laid bare. A group of the Companions and Followers of the Interpretation said: It will reveal a serious matter. Who said that? Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Usama bin Zaid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The day the shin will be uncovered. He said: It is a day of war and hardship. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On the Day when the shin will be laid bare. He said: About a great matter, like the poet’s saying: The war started against us Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: On the Day when the shin will be laid bare, and no believer will remain but will prostrate, and the back of the unbeliever will harden and become a single bone. Ibn Abbas used to say: A great matter will be laid bare. Haven’t you heard the Arabs say: The war started against us Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, On the Day when the shin will be laid bare, meaning: when the matter will be laid bare and the deeds will be made apparent, and its being laid bare: entering the Hereafter and the matter being laid bare from him. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, On the Day the shin will be laid bare is the severe and terrifying matter of terror on the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi and Ibn Hamid told me: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, On the Day when the shin will be laid bare, he said: The severity and seriousness of the matter. Ibn Abbas said: It is the most intense hour on the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: The severity of the matter, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, On the Day when the shin will be laid bare, he said: The severity of the matter, Ibn Abbas said: It is the first hour that will be on the Day of Resurrection, except that in the hadith of Al-Harith he said: And Ibn Abbas said: It is the most severe hour that will be on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim ibn Kulayb, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said: About the severity of the matter. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, On the Day the shin will be laid bare, he said: About a terrible and grave matter. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, On the Day the shin will be laid bare, he said: On the Day the severity of the matter will be laid bare. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, On the Day when the shin will be uncovered, and Ibn Abbas used to say: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to say, War has rolled up its shin, meaning the coming of the Hereafter and the passing of this world. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated: Abd al-Rahman narrated: Sufyan narrated: Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated: Abu al-Zahra’ narrated: Abdullah said: God will appear to His creation on the Day of Resurrection until the Muslims pass by. He said: Then He will say: Who do you worship? They will say: We worship God and do not associate anything with Him. Then He will rebuke them two or three times, saying: Do you know your Lord? They will say: Our Lord. Then He will say: You were called to prostration while you were safe. Yahya ibn Talha al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of al-Minhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: A crier will call out on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:'Is it not just from your Lord, Who created you, then shaped you, then provided for you, then you turned away from Him, that He should appoint every servant among you as he appointed?' They will say: 'Yes.' He said: Then the gods they used to worship will be presented to every people, and they will tire them out and they will lead them to the Fire. But the people of the call will remain, and some of them will say to one another: 'What are you waiting for?' The people will go away, and they will say: 'We are waiting for Him to call us.' So He will come to them in a form.' He said: 'He will mention whatever God wills of it, and He will reveal whatever He wills to reveal.' He said: 'They will fall down in prostration except for the hypocrites, for the backbone of their loins will become a single bone like the rumps of cows, and it will be said to them: 'Raise your heads toward your light.' Then he mentioned a long story. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, he said: Al-A'mash narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Qays ibn Sakin, he said: Abdullah narrated to Umar while he was with him, On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds (al-Mutaffifin 83:6), he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, he said: The people will stand before the Lord of the worlds for forty years, their eyes fixed on the heavens, barefoot and naked, bridled with sweat, and no human being will speak to them for forty years. Then a caller will call out: O mankind, is it not just from your Lord, who created you and shaped you and provided for you, then you worshipped other than Him, that He should give every people what they had taken? They said: Yes. He said: Then what they used to worship besides God will be presented to every people, meaning their gods, and they will follow them until they are thrown into the Fire, and only the Muslims and the hypocrites will remain. Then it will be said: Will you not go away, for the people have gone away? They will say: Until our Lord comes to us. He will say: And will you recognize Him? They said: If he confesses to us. He said: Then He will appear and those who used to worship Him will fall down in prostration. He said: And the hypocrites will remain, unable to do so, as if there are skewers on their backs. He said: Then He will take them and drive them to the Fire, and they will be thrown down, and these people will enter Paradise. He said: Then they will be met in Paradise with what they will be met with of reward, wives, and wide-eyed maidens. Each man of them will be in Paradise with such and such, between each Paradise is such and such, between the nearest and the farthest is a thousand years, and he will see the farthest as he sees the nearest. He said: And a man of good appearance will meet him, and if he looks at him coming, he will think that he is his Lord, and he will say to him: Do not do that, I am only your servant and your commander over a thousand villages. He said: Umar will say: O Ka’b, do you not hear what Abdullah is talking about? Ibn Jabalah narrated: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated: Abu Uwanah narrated: Sulayman al-A'mash narrated: Al-Munhal ibn Amr narrated: Abu Ubaydah and Qays ibn Sakn narrated: Abdullah said while he was speaking to Umar: Umar kept saying: Woe to you, Ka'b! Don't you hear what Abdullah is saying? When the people are gathered on their feet for forty years, their eyes fixed on the sky, no one will speak to them, and the sun will be over their heads until sweat bridles them, all of them righteous and wicked. Then a voice from the sky will call out: "O mankind, is it not just from your Lord, who created you, provided for you, and shaped you, then you turned away from other than Him, that every man among you should be given what he was given? They will say: "Yes." Then a voice from the sky will call out: "O mankind, let every nation set out to do what it used to worship." A mirage will be spread out for them. What they used to worship will be made visible to them. They will set out until they enter the Fire. Then it will be said to the Muslims: "What is holding you back?" They say: This is our place until our Lord comes to us. Then it is said to them: Will you recognize Him if you see Him? They say: If He confesses to us, we will recognize Him. He said: Abu Salih narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that one of them would turn around and uncover his shin, and they would fall down in prostration. He said: The backs of the hypocrites will be fused together until they become a single bone, like the rumps of cows. He said: It will be said to them: Raise your heads to your light in proportion to your deeds. He said: A group of them will raise their heads to light like mountains, and they will pass over the Sirat like the blink of an eye. Then another group will raise their heads to things like palaces, and they will pass over the Sirat like the wind. Then others will raise before them things like houses, and they will pass like horses. Then others will be raised to a light less than that, and they will pull themselves up tightly, and others less than that will walk, until the last of the people will remain, a man on the tip of his toe like a lamp, and he will fall down one time and straighten up another time, and the fire will strike him and it will scatter from him until he comes out, and he will say: No one has been given what I have been given, and he does not know from what he was saved, except that I felt its touch, and I felt its heat. And he mentioned a long hadith, from which I have shortened this. Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, on the authority of Ata' ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: 'Let every nation join what it used to worship.' No one who used to worship an idol, a statue, or an image will remain, except that they will go until they fall into the Fire. Only those who used to worship God alone will remain, from the righteous and the wicked, and the dust of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be presented as if it were a mirage, one part crushing the other. Then the Jews will be called, and it will be said to them: 'What did you worship?' They will say: 'Uzair, the son of God.' He will say: 'You have lied. God has not taken a wife or a son. So what do you want?' They will say: 'O our Lord, we are thirsty.' He will say: 'Will you not then return?' They will go until they fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be called, and it will be said: 'What did you worship?' They will say: 'The Messiah, the son of God.'" He will say, “You have lied. God has not taken a wife or a son. What do you want?” They will say, O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us something to drink. He will say, Will you not then be returned? They will go and fall into the Fire, and only those who used to worship God, both the righteous and the wicked, will remain. He said, “Then God will appear to us in a form other than the one in which we saw Him the first time, and He will say, ‘O people, every nation has followed what it used to worship, and you will remain.’ On that Day, none will speak to Him except the prophets. They will say, ‘We left the people in this world, and we were more in need of their company therein. Every nation has followed what it used to worship, and we are awaiting our Lord whom we used to worship.’ He will say, “I am your Lord.” They will say, We seek refuge in God from you. He will say, Is there a sign between you and God by which you recognize Him? They will say, Yes. He will uncover his shin, and they will all fall down in prostration. There will not remain anyone who had prostrated in this world for the sake of showing off, or showing off, or hypocrisy, except that his back will become a single plate. Every time he wants to prostrate, he will fall on his back. He will say, “Then he will return, raising up our righteous and our wrongdoers, and he will be equal to us in the form in which we saw him the first time. He will say, ‘I am your Lord.’ They will say, ‘Yes, you are our Lord,’” three times. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me: My father and Saeed ibn al-Layth told me: Khalid ibn Yazid told us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “His crier will call out and say: ‘Let every people join what they used to worship.’ So the people of the cross will go with their cross, and the people of idols with their idols, and the people of every god with their gods, until there remains whoever used to worship God, from the righteous and the wicked, and the remnants of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be brought forth and displayed as if it were a mirage.” Then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Then we await our Lord. He said: If he said it, then the Almighty will come to them. Then he told us a hadith similar to the hadith of al-Masruqi. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will take revenge for the oppressed from the oppressor until no one remains accountable to anyone. Then God will appoint an angel from the angels in the image of Uzair, and the Jews will follow him. Then God will appoint an angel from the angels in the image of Jesus, and the Christians will follow him. Then a caller will call out that will be heard by all of creation, saying: ‘Let every people join their gods and what they used to worship besides God. ’ No one who used to worship anything besides God will remain without his gods being presented to him before him. Then they will be led to the Fire until no one remains except the believers, among whom are the hypocrites. Then God, the Most High, will say: ‘O people, the people have gone, the people have gone. Join your gods and what you used to worship. ’ They will say: ‘By God, we have no god but God, and we did not worship any god other than Him. ’ But it is God who made them steadfast. Then He will say to them a second time in the same way: ‘Join your gods and what you used to worship. ’” Do you worship? They will say the same, and it will be said: Is there a sign between you and your Lord that you recognize?
