They will say: Yes, and His greatness will be revealed to them, so that they will know that He is their Lord, and they will fall down on their faces in prostration before Him, and every hypocrite will fall on his back, and God will make their backs like the hooves of cows.” Abu Zaid Umar ibn Shabah told me, saying: Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, saying: Abu Saeed Ruh ibn Janah told us, on the authority of a client of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: On the Day the shin will be laid bare, he said: On the Day of a great light, before which they will fall down in prostration. Jaafar bin Muhammad Al-Bazuri told me: Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding the statement of God, On the Day the shin will be laid bare, he said: The covering will be laid bare. He said: And they will be called to prostrate while they are safe. Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, The Day the shin will be laid bare, he said: It is a day of distress and hardship. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he had read it as, The Day the shin will be laid bare, meaning: The Day the Resurrection will reveal severe hardship. The Arabs say, This matter was laid bare from the shin, if it became severe. From this comes the saying of the poet: She showed them her leg and it was clear that she was evil. His saying, And they are called to prostrate, but they are unable to do so, means: And they are called to uncover their shins in order to prostrate to God Almighty, but they are unable to do so.
68:43: And His statement: Their eyes will be humbled, humiliation will cover them. He says: humiliation from the punishment of God will cover them. And they were called to prostrate while they were healthy. He says: And in this world, they were called to prostrate to Him while they were healthy, with nothing preventing them from doing so, and nothing standing between Him and them. It has been said: Prostration in this context is the obligatory prayer. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taimi: And they were called to prostration while they were healthy. He said: To the obligatory prayer. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And they were called to prostration. He said: He hears the caller to the obligatory prayer but does not answer him. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi, And they were called to prostration. He said: The obligatory prayer. And similar to what we said about His statement, They are called to prostrate, but they are unable... the verse, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And they used to be called to prostration while they were safe, he said: They are the disbelievers who used to call upon Him in this world while they were safe. So today He is calling upon them while they are afraid. Then God, the Exalted, informed us that He will stand between the polytheists and His obedience in this world and the Hereafter. As for in this world, He said, They could not hear, nor could they see (Hud 11:20). As for the Hereafter, He said, So they cannot, * Their eyes will be downcast. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: They will be called to prostrate, but they will not be able to, that is, by God, on the Day of Resurrection. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Permission will be given to the believers on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate, so the believers will prostrate, and among every believer will be a hypocrite, so the back of the hypocrite will harden from prostrating, and God will make the prostration of the believers towards them a rebuke, humiliation, degradation, regret, and sorrow.” His saying, And they were called to prostration, meaning in this world, and they were safe, meaning in this world. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It has reached me that permission will be given to the believers on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate among every believer a hypocrite. The believers will prostrate, but the hypocrite will not be able to prostrate. I think he said: Their backs will harden, and the prostration of the believers will be a rebuke to them. He said: And they were called to prostrate while they were safe.
68:44: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, I entrust the affair of these deniers of the Qur’an to Him. This is like someone saying to another person threatening a man: Leave me and him alone, meaning that he is behind his harm. Min in His statement, And whoever denies this hadith, is in the accusative case, because the meaning of the statement is what I mentioned. It is similar to their saying, If I left you to your own opinion, you would not succeed. The Arabs place the accusative case on your opinion because the meaning of the statement is: If I left you to your own opinion, you would not succeed. And His statement: We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know, God Almighty says: We will plot against them from where they do not know, by giving them enjoyment of worldly pleasures until they think that their enjoyment of them is better for them with God, so they persist in their transgression, then He will seize them suddenly while they do not perceive.
68:45: And His statement: “And I will grant them respite. Indeed, My plan is firm.” God Almighty says: And I will extend their terms for a period of time, and that is for a period of time, due to their disbelief and rebellion against God, so that God’s arguments against them may be complete. Indeed, My plan is firm. He says: Indeed, My plan against the people of disbelief is strong and severe.
68:46: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, do you ask these polytheists for a reward and recompense for what you have given them of advice and called them to the truth? “They are burdened with a heavy fine. That is, they are burdened with the fine for that reward, and the burden of paying it has burdened them, so they refrained from accepting your advice and avoided, due to the great burden of the fine that had befallen them, and what you asked them for that was to enter into the religion to which you called them.
68:47: And His statement: Or do they have the unseen, so they write it down? He says: Do they have the Preserved Tablet, in which is the report of what will happen, so they write down what is in it, and argue with you about it, and claim that, despite their disbelief in their Lord, they have a better status with God than the people of faith in Him.
68:48: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So be patient, O Muhammad, for the decree and judgment of your Lord concerning you and these polytheists, with what you have brought them of this Qur’an and this religion. Continue with what your Lord has commanded you to do, and do not let their denial of you and their harm to you prevent you from conveying what you have been commanded to convey. And His saying: And do not be like the companion of the fish who was imprisoned in its belly, and he is Jonah, son of Matta, peace be upon him, so your Lord will punish you for not conveying that, just as He punished him by imprisoning him in its belly when he called out while he was distressed meaning: when he called out while he was sad, and sadness had weighed him down and he was swallowing it. As Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, When he called out, full of grief, meaning: sorrowful. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Deeply distressed, he said: Sorrowful. Qatada used to say about his statement, And do not be like the companion of the fish,: Do not be like him in haste and anger. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So be patient over the decision of your Lord and do not be like the companion of the fish when he cried out in anguish. He said: Do not be hasty as he was hasty, and do not become angry as he became angry. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same.
68:49: And His saying: Had it not been for the grace of his Lord overtaking him, God Almighty says: Had it not been for the owner of the house overtaking a grace from his Lord, who had mercy on him with it, and accepted his repentance for his anger at his Lord, he would have been thrown into the open, which is the open space of the earth. And from this is the saying of Qays ibn Ja’dah: I raised my feet, not fearing their stumbling, and threw my clothes in the open country. And it is blameworthy. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying and it is blameworthy. Some of them said: It means: and he is blameworthy. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and he is blameworthy, he said: and he is blameworthy. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He is guilty. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Bakr: And he is blameworthy. He said: And he is a sinner.
68:50: God Almighty says: So his Lord chose the companion of the fish, meaning He selected him and chose him for his prophethood. And made him among the righteous, meaning among the messengers who acted according to what their Lord commanded them to do and refrained from what He forbade them from doing.
68:51: And His statement: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes God Almighty says: And indeed, O Muhammad, those who disbelieve would almost pierce you with their eyes because of the intensity of their enmity towards you and they would remove you and throw you when they look at you out of rage against you. It has been said that what is meant by that is: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost throw you, O Muhammad, and overthrow you, as the Arabs say: So-and-so almost overthrew me with the intensity of his looks at me. They said: The Quraysh only attacked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in order to cast the evil eye on him, so they looked at him to help him and said: We have never seen a man like him, or he is mad. So God said to His Prophet at that time: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost throw you with their eyes" when they heard the message and they say: He is mad. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of to make you slip, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the message, meaning: They would pierce you with their eyes from the intensity of their gaze. Ibn Abbas said: It is said of the aral-Saff 61:The arrow has slipped or slipped. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, that they may make you slip with their eyes, meaning: that they may make you slip with their eyes. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes, meaning: they would almost make you slip with their eyes. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, that he used to recite And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost destroy you. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, to make you slip, he said: to make you slip with their eyes. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, to make you slip with their eyes, he said: to destroy you. Al-Kalbi said: to overthrow you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes to pierce you with their eyes, in enmity towards the Book of God and the remembrance of God. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes, meaning: They would make you slip with their eyes out of enmity and hatred. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, li-zilaqunak. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as li-zilaqunak with a fat-ha on the ya from zalatuhu zalqan. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as li-zilaqunak with a damma on the ya from azlaquhu yazlaquhu. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings and two famous dialects among the Arabs, with similar meanings. The Arabs say to someone who shaves his head: he made him slip and he made him slip, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And His statement: When they heard the message, meaning when they heard the Book of God being recited, and they say, ‘Indeed, he is mad,’ God Almighty says: These polytheists, whose characteristics He described, say, Muhammad is mad, and what he brought us is the delirium that he raves about in his madness.
68:52: And it is only a reminder to the worlds. Muhammad is only a reminder through which God reminded the two worlds, the jinn and mankind.
